result.title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
result.summary: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. Coding agents make task-specific programs cheap to write, but not efficient ones easy to find: whether a computational strategy is accurate and fast enough becomes clear only after it actually runs at the target scale. We introduce BORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. BORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, BORN unfolds the preset schemes of existing packages into independently configurable algorithmic components, selects the fastest strategy within the error tolerance from the predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, and guides coding agents to compile it with component-level performance predictions. For a Hartree-Fock calculation with 50,024 basis functions, BORN finishes in 1.41h on a single CPU node, 77$\times$ faster than the estimated runtime of a general-purpose baseline and still 9.8$\times$ faster with development time included. On a single GPU, BORN completes the ubiquitin calculation in 2.1,h, the same order of runtime as the GPU-accelerated package Mako on 64 GPUs, and shortens the B-DNA duplex calculation from an estimated two months to 8.1,h (173$\times$).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BORN 前瞻式 agentic 计算框架：在运行前由小规模体系外推误差、结合目标规模负载与实测硬件吞吐预测耗时，据此在精度-时间 Pareto 前沿上选取策略，并指导编码 agent 生成高性能量子化学程序。
AI.relevance_reason: 「先预测误差与成本、再决定执行哪种策略」与 LVR 中推理路径、计算深度选择和停止决策的收益-成本预估可能有概念联系，可供核查；但论文不涉及视觉证据或 latent 状态机制。
